Question: How should one deal with this at a restaurant, ordering a steak dinner with baked potato and actually being served instant potatoes instead, and the manager saying they had run out of baked potatoes?

While many restaurants do have a clause on the menu in fine print that states substitutions may be made or something to that effect, that clause really should only be used as a shield from abusive customers. It should never be a restaurants policy. As a food server I would not be happy and I would really expect the manager to comp the meal (give for free) or at the least give a free dessert or something to the customer if they served them a plate of food they changed without asking first. If they did not do that minor bit of an apology I would start looking for another place to work. Since restaurants do not pay much and I had to rely on tips I need to work in a place that lets me earn as much as I can, not tie my hands. Honestly even if they just honored my request without apology I’d still probably not come back. Now if the manager apologized and offered me a token like a free dessert I would surely come back.
